description: Cut the redundant D2D memory traffic and small-kernel launch overhead on the routing/peel glue, a bottleneck no worker has touched. brief-49 profiling measured ~5.16ms of D2D memcpy on shape 11 (index_select / cat / .contiguous copies) plus many small gather/scatter/elementwise launches across shapes 3/6/7/8 from the mixed-peel and low-rank routing. Eliminate the copies: fuse the per-subset gather+scatter, operate on views / index tensors instead of materializing contiguous sub-batches, preallocate and reuse scratch, and coalesce the small elementwise ops. Pure torch, structural (access-pattern + redundant-work), orthogonal to the in-flight sign-DC/block-eigh kernels.

t1: anti-alias baddbmm in sign-DC (shape 11). Removed aliased torch.baddbmm(X,X,X2)/(M,X,M) copies in _sign_dc_solve NS-sign loop + P+/P- projectors + right-side trsm in _sign_dc_cqr. Shape-11 D2D memcpy 28ops/16570MB/5142us -> 3ops/789MB/252us (-95% bytes/-95% time). Wall-clock flat: geomean 31109->31202us, shape11 109660->109480us (D2D was overlapped w/ cuSOLVER base solve, not on critical path). Math-identical. 39/39 valid, 0 fallback, stream absent.

t2: anti-alias baddbmm in n=2048 sign-DC (_sign_dc_block_eigh + _sign_dc_multiway). Shape-5 D2D 46ops/5174MB/1614us -> 6ops/293MB/101us (-94%). Wall-clock flat: geomean 31109->31140us, shape5 109587->109500us. Shape5 38% GPU-idle is cuSOLVER per-matrix syevd launch latency (b8, two ~1117 halves), not the overlapped D2D. Math-identical, 39/39 valid, 0 fallback, stream absent.

t3: coalesce mixed-peel-gate syncs (2 .item() -> 1 .tolist()) on shape 6. geomean 31109->31145us (flat), shape6 flat. MEASURED shape-6 idle breakdown: 12.4ms inter-kernel gap = 7.8ms cuSOLVER per-matrix syevd launch latency (unremovable glue-external) + 2.6ms routing/subset stalls + 1.9ms medium. Peel-gate syncs are not the bottleneck. 39/39 valid, 0 fallback, stream absent.

HEAD=ce5786fdf0612d3961936c2b6cfcc90618b87b2e, geomean 31138us (baseline 31109, +0.09% = noise; parent metric 31127). 3 trials, all 39/39 valid, 0 new fallback, stream absent. NAILED the brief's cited signal but it did NOT convert to wall-clock.

ROOT CAUSE of the shape-11 5.16ms D2D (nailed via NVTX+sync attribution): NOT the gather/cat/contiguous glue the brief hypothesized -- it was ALIASED torch.baddbmm in the sign-DC Newton-Schulz sign loop. torch.baddbmm(X,X,X2,beta=1.5) aliases bias(X)==batch1(X), so cuBLAS D2D-COPIES X (671MB) into the fresh output before the beta accumulate, once PER NS iter (20x) + the P+/P- projector applications; ditto the n=2048 path (_sign_dc_block_eigh, 32x134MB). t1 (shape11) + t2 (shape5) split each into Y=scale*X then Y.baddbmm_(...) (fused GEMM kept). MEASURED D2D: shape11 28ops/16570MB/5142us -> 3ops/789MB/245us (-95%); shape5 46ops/5174MB/1614us -> 6ops/293MB/101us (-94%). Math-identical (same ops/order/TF32). t3 coalesced the mixed-peel-gate .item() syncs (2->1).

WHY FLAT: the copies were fully EXPOSED (single stream, not overlapped) -- but they are INTRINSIC WORK, not redundant. The '1.5*X' term of NS is one 671MB bandwidth pass whether done as the aliased copy (parent) or my mul (671MB read+write, same cost). Removing the copy raised kernel-busy +6.9ms (the mul) while cutting memcpy -4.9ms -> net flat. There is NO copy-free formulation: 1.5X-0.5*X@X2 forces bias to alias a GEMM operand. So the brief's premise 'redundant D2D round-trips' is REFUTED for the sign-DC NS loop -- measured, not reasoned.

IDLE MAP (GPU-busy/wall, one call): shape11 2.3% idle, shape8 3.1% (both COMPUTE-BOUND -> no glue headroom); shape6 9.3%, shape7 17.3%, shape5 38.4% (SMALL-BATCH, idle dominated by cuSOLVER per-matrix syevd LAUNCH LATENCY: shape6's 12.4ms inter-kernel gap = 7.8ms of <5us gaps across ~250 'rest' syevd matrices + only 2.6ms routing/subset stalls). That launch latency is torch.linalg.eigh-internal, NOT removable glue. The index_select().contiguous() the brief flagged is a documented NO-OP (index_select already contiguous; verified data_ptr unchanged).

OPEN DIRECTIONS (unexplored, for the manager): (1) shapes 5/6/7 idle is cuSOLVER launch latency at small batch -- the ONLY way to reclaim it is to move the 'rest'/whole-batch cuSOLVER eigh off per-matrix syevd (a batched dense eigensolver / the megakernel for the rest subset) -- ALGORITHMIC, out of this brief's glue scope. (2) shape7 (mixed1024, 17% idle) wastes a full _lr_participation_ratio A@A + _twolevel_mask probe before landing on plain cuSOLVER -- can't skip (reseed-unsafe shape key) but a cheaper concentration probe than full A@A might shave ~0.5-1ms. (3) The remaining shape11 786MB CQR trsm copy + shape8's 12 low-rank-CQR copies look cuSOLVER-batched-trsm-internal (unremovable from torch). (4) t1/t2's mul is marginally worse than the aliased copy on bandwidth-bound shapes; if the manager wants pure no-regression, REVERT t1/t2 and keep only t3 (or revert all -- the D2D byte-reduction has no wall-clock value since it's intrinsic). Recommend: keep t3 (clean sync coalesce), treat t1/t2 as a measured refutation that this brief's lever is not wall-clock-actionable.
